main_chase_cards.name: Dark Fearow
main_chase_cards.why: Dark Fearow is the book-route bird at the edge of Pokemon Card GB2. It is not packed with the cartridge like Team GR's Mewtwo and Lugia; it comes through the official guidebook, which makes it a different kind of contact object: paper explaining software, carrying cardboard that points back to both.

claims.text: The local catalog and Bulbapedia align on April 12, 2001 for the Pokemon Card GB2: Here Comes Team GR! Official Guidebook insert route; PokeBoon gives the guidebook release as 2001/04/13, so the catalog keeps April 12 as the row date and records the day-level discrepancy as a source caution.
Bulbapedia states Dark Fearow was available as an unnumbered promotional card in copies of the Pokemon Card GB2: Here Comes Team GR! Official Guidebook.
The local release family models one row: Dark Fearow source index 229, with the promotion note Pokemon Card GB2: Here Comes Team GR! Official Guidebook insert.

PokeBoon identifies the guidebook as a Media Factory book edited by the Pokemon Card Trainers Editorial Department, 207 pages, and related to the Great Rocket's Mewtwo and Lugia Pokemon Card GB2 insert promos.
Bulbapedia states Dark Fearow has a GB symbol in place of an expansion symbol and that the bottom border reads "Pokemon Card GB2 Official Guidebook" bonus card.

Bulbapedia credits Sumiyoshi Kizuki / 木月すみよし for Dark Fearow, while PokeBoon credits Naoyo Kimura / 木村直代; this source-set treats the illustrator as a source conflict requiring card-image confirmation.

Dark Fearow matters because it is the guidebook leg of the Pokemon Card GB2 promo cluster: an explanatory book about a digital TCG sequel that carries its own old-back card, distinct from the game-box Team GR's Mewtwo and Lugia inserts.

narrative.human_title: Pokemon Card GB2 guidebook — Dark Fearow as the book-route bird
narrative.why_it_matters: Dark Fearow is the quieter sibling to the cartridge pack-ins, and that is the interesting part. Team GR's Mewtwo and Lugia came with the game; Dark Fearow came with the guidebook, the paper object that taught players how to move through Team GR's digital world. It is a card about routes: software explained by a book, a book carrying a card, and a GB symbol tying the whole little circuit together.

narrative.human_title: Dark Fearow — source index 229, the GB guidebook bird
narrative.why_it_matters: Dark Fearow is not the cartridge prize; it is the guidebook bird, and that makes it a different kind of artifact. It belongs to the moment when Pokemon Card GB2 needed paper maps, strategy pages, and a physical bonus card to complete the experience. Even the illustrator conflict becomes part of the charm for an agentic catalog: do not merely recite a name, look at the printed card and let the object settle the claim.
